subject: POC: Prompt set + eval plan (next steps and success criteria)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@scopetech.com>, Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@scopetech.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: POC: Prompt set + eval plan (next steps and success criteria)

Hi Emily / Paul —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and helpful context on the ScopeTech search & assist workflow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC moving: 

Success criteria (what we’ll measure during the trial):
- Relevance: top-1 answer accuracy on your labeled eval set >= 72% (you can adjust).
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 450ms for the typical prompt size you described (~80 tokens).
- Cost: incremental per-request token cost vs baseline (we’ll provide estimated units).
- Qualitative: product-team sign-off on response usefulness for 20 sampled prompts.

POC intake we need from you (can be a single tarball/S3 drop):
1) Prompt set & eval labels (CSV) — example format in attached sample_eval_prompts.txt
2) Representative request logs (redacted) for 2 weeks: columns you mentioned (user_id, timestamp, prompt_text, result_id, rubric_label)
3) Any instruction/system prompts, temperature, top_k/top_p settings you use in prod
4) A named owner for the POC on your side (who we’ll coordinate with)

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (kickoff): intake + access (this week)
- Week 1: data ingestion + baseline runs + initial metric report
- Week 2: tuning (prompt templates, config) + human sample review
- Week 3: final report + recommendations + handoff

Can you confirm the owner who will share the prompt CSV/logs, and whether S3 is OK for secure upload? I’ve attached our Redwood POC template (redwood_poc_template.xlsx) and a short sample prompt format (sample_eval_prompts.txt) to make it easier.

Preferred kickoff windows: Tue 3/17 or Wed 3/18 morning PST.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20m if that helps.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@scopetech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@scopetech.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt set + eval plan (next steps and success criteria)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed.

Owner: Paul will own the data share and is looped here. We will provide a CSV of ~3k prompts and a subset of redacted logs (we’ll remove PII before sending). S3 is preferred for transfer — we can drop to an account path you provide.

On success criteria: the product team is mostly focused on relevance and latency; the cost metric is secondary but helpful. We have an existing DPA but can sign any additional transfer agreements if required.

I’ll ask Paul to push the prompt file by Friday 3/12 EOD.

Emily Turner
Head of ML | ScopeTech
emily.turner@scopetech.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC intake (technical checklist)

Marissa / team — quick technical intake items so we can scope the POC correctly: 
- Prompt CSV: columns we need: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_label (optional), category/tag. If there are system prompts, include them as separate rows or a header field.
- Logs: redacted user_id is fine; timestamps in ISO; indicate any preprocessing currently applied.
- Metrics: propose we compute exact-match / BLEU / embedding-similarity thresholds and include a small human-blind A/B sample for qualitative scoring.
- Volume: please confirm expected peak QPS for the trial (estimate). If >50 QPS we’ll need to size Dedicated or a temporary burst config.
- File formats: we can ingest CSV/JSONL; compressed (gz) is fine.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for ingestion and baseline scripts once we have the sample files.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@scopetech.com>, Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@scopetech.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt set + eval plan (next steps and success criteria)

Thanks Emily — great, Paul thanks in advance for taking point. A couple quick notes: 
- We checked our records and the DPA in your onboarding folder covers data processing; I’ll send a copy to Paul via HubSpot. If you need a separate agreement for transfer, we can route to legal quickly.
- Kickoff: let’s target Tue 3/17 10:00 AM PST — I’ll book a 30m kickoff for the core team (Aditya for technical, Vivek for success).

Proposed POC milestones (short):
1) Intake & validation (3/17) — you drop prompt CSV + logs to the S3 path below; Aditya will validate schema.
2) Baseline run (3/18–3/19) — Redwood runs eval across your prompts; deliver baseline metrics.
3) Iteration (3/22–3/24) — tuning & config; human sample review.
4) Final report (3/26) — recommendations and next steps.

Secure upload (please drop files here): s3://scopetech-secure-transfer/poc/2026/03/

Attached: poc_eval_plan_v1.pdf and our redwood_poc_template.xlsx.

If that works, Paul — please confirm and share when you’ll push the file.

Best,
Marissa
From: Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@scopetech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Turner <emily.turner@scopetech.com>

Date: 2026-03-15T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt set + eval plan (next steps and success criteria)

Marissa / team — attaching the prompt set + sample logs we discussed. We redacted PII and kept user_id hashed. The CSV includes columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_label, category, timestamp, hashed_user_id, model_response, human_label (where available).

Attachment: scopetech_prompts_and_logs_20260312.csv (gzipped, ~18MB)

Notes / questions:
- We compressed the CSV (gz) — you mentioned compressed is fine.
- Two example prompt types to flag: 
  * "Search query correction" prompts (short queries, often noisy)
  * "Assist: summarize & suggest actions" (longer, structured responses required)

We can confirm kickoff 3/17 10:00 AM PST. I’ll be the primary on our side for the POC and will coordinate any access. Do you have a contact at Redwood for compliance/DPA follow-up?

—Paul Jenkins
Principal ML Engineer | ScopeTech
